0a4c42fef9ba5de701ea.text: Using Conditionals (Zero, First, Second and Third

bed2353595edecc36da4.text: In your previous lessons, you have learned about conditionals and its type

5526460ef6888375a547.text: and usage. As a review, a Conditional sentence is a type of sentence that expresses a condition and the outcome or the result of that condition. A condition is something that can occur IF something else happens.

289c00b513afe8978ae9.text: A Conditional sentence is of a dependent clause and an independent clause

e4cd587bc29f9d3a871f.text: that are put together to express the condition and the result.

edaad6f7fbeb1a977db2.text: If you stay at home, you will be safer from the threat of the pandemic.

755a9804ab1c0ead0e65.text: The if-clause tells you the condition (If you stay at home) and the main clause tells you the result (you will be safer from the threat of the pandemic).

460fb824ba795b542597.text: We use the zero conditional to talk about things about general truth, especially for laws and rules.

87aa5eb8cf49953c668e.text: We use the first conditional when we talk about the future situation that is possible to happen or can happen in reality.

9f5e53936d7d73e0cc46.text: The second conditional is used to express the present or future situation that is impossible or unlikely to happen in reality.

19851fa2b91d13bef275.text: The third conditional is used to refer to a time that is in the pastor unreal past condition and express its probable past result.

058f54980da2ba7cbcbe.text: Conditional sentences are also used to express arguments. Arguments are

51130095cdfa502d0665.text: statements expressing a reason or set of reasons given to persuade others that a certain action or given idea is right or wrong. It is also used to deliver or to present a reason or reasons why you support or oppose an idea or suggestion.

b2eeb459ddff93f84787.text: In expressing arguments using conditional sentences, you are going to present

46d437c2d0f515c408a8.text: your response as the result from a given condition (if-clause) and/or you will tell the possible or the probable cause of a certain situation or result (main-clause).

1443a0a9a071bb013d4d.text: Situation: Mary’s teacher sent a reminder in their class’ group chat that the

d8e0d43aad5b4fb87bbe.text: submission of their module would be on the day after next. John, one of her classmates, asked her to send him her answer because he forgot to work on his module. If you were Mary, would you help John finish his module by sending him your answers? Why or why not?

183d6f2c5f0e42b61c3f.text: Possible Answer: If I were Mary, I would help John finish his module, but I would not

36749f3f7c17d4c2aeb0.text: send him my answers. I would tell him to start doing his module now and help him out in understanding the lesson. I would also motivate him to answer his module ahead of time so he would not cram the night before the submission.

30955b3b14e03b598bc9.text: Make sure to use the correct type of conditional based on the form/tense of

523c32ac84e138de8fee.text: the verb given on the question/situation.
